headline: London Reservoir's Floating Solar Farm Proves a Decade of Clean Power
meta_description: Over 23,000 solar panels have floated on a London reservoir for 10 years, generating 5.8 million kWh of clean electricity annually while using less than 10% of…
summary_short: A decade-long experiment in floating solar power on a London reservoir shows clean energy and water management can work together efficiently.
body:
More than 23,000 solar panels have been floating on a London reservoir for a full decade, quietly proving that clean energy and water management can coexist. The installation generates 5.8 million kilowatt-hours of electricity every year—enough to power thousands of homes—while covering less than 10% of the reservoir's surface.

What makes this achievement remarkable is its efficiency: the panels accomplish significant energy production without dominating the waterway or disrupting its primary function. By placing solar infrastructure on water rather than land, the project demonstrates a smart use of existing spaces that might otherwise remain untapped for renewable energy.

A decade of continuous operation suggests floating solar technology is more than experimental—it's proven, reliable, and scalable. As communities worldwide search for ways to meet climate goals without consuming additional land, projects like this London reservoir become a practical blueprint for combining water management with the clean energy transition.
quick_facts: 23,000+ solar panels installed on a London reservoir
5.8 million kWh of clean electricity generated annually
Less than 10% of the water's surface covered
